# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Headless `fa -p` DRAINS live shell
  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  shell-job-scoped kill switch: live shell jobs detach at once while the
  pre-existing subagent drain stays unconditional), then the detach
  summary applies (gh-1459). The drain wrap-up also raises the
  settle→reaction fence: from `_finishHeadlessDrain` on, a job settle (or
  task completion) does bookkeeping only — no reaction run (gh-1589 I2).
  While the drain waits, every `headless.shellJobQuietMs`
  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE
  interim liveness notice (`job <id> running · <elapsed> · tail: …` +
  the bash_job escape hatch), skipped for a crossing the model probed
  itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe generation)
  (gh-1459 ask #4). The headless `finally` then closes the session with
  the SEAL (`Session.seal`, gh-1589): after the usage fold + the
  job-board/obligations/subagent flushes (close order: drain → usage
  fold → seal → exit, the REPL teardown seals the same way), every writer
  observes the sealed session — late appends are DROPPED with one stderr
  warning per writer class, never written, so the session JSONL is a
  sealed artifact before the process exits. The seal is per-run state
  (a resume opens the same file unsealed); the harbor adapter mirrors the
  contract from the outside: `run()` returns only after the fa process
  exited (kill + bounded reap on every path, incl. external cancel; loud
  degradation when the reap times out). Job logs on disk are NOT
  secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`
  (`default|pi|omp`) pick the tool-LOAD preset — `default` loads every
  enabled tool; `pi` the 4-tool benchmark base (issue #679, discovery
  off); `omp` the essential base with everything else discoverable,
  mounted on demand through the omp-only `discover_tools` meta tool (an
  explicit `tools: {id: on}` is a standing mount). The gate's
  `discoveryEnabled` flag keeps the discoverable tombstone from
  dead-ending on `discover_tools` in modes that don't register it. CLI
  sync + `/settings` switch in `agent_cli_tools.dart`/`settings_flow.dart`;
  user-facing docs: docs/tool-availability.md §Load modes.
- `lib/src/lsp/` — `lsp` tool (diagnostics/definition/references/rename):
  pure-Dart JSON-RPC client over `LspTransport`; `.dart` →
  `dart language-server --protocol=lsp`, projects merge `.fah/lsp.json`;
  lazy start, 5-min idle shutdown, crash respawn with backoff; renames apply
  all-or-nothing through the env. IO transport only via `lib/io.dart` +
  `builtinTools(env, lsp:)`; 1-indexed line/character; missing server =
  clean note, never a crash.
- `lib/src/mcp/` — MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers from the `mcp:`
  section of `~/.fah/config.yaml` (strict `ConfigException` parsing; config
  file only, no CLI commands). Stdio (`command`/`args`/`env`,
  newline-delimited JSON-RPC — NOT LSP's Content-Length framing) and remote
  (`url`, streamable-http default or legacy sse, `headers`). Message-level
  `McpTransport`; stdio framing glue is pure Dart over `McpByteChannel`
  (process impl only via `lib/io.dart`), both HTTP transports are pure Dart
  over injectable `package:http` (web gets remote servers; stdio = clean
  "not supported" status). `McpManager` connects lazily in the background
  (boot never blocks), per-server connecting/connected/failed status,
  reconnect with capped backoff; tools register as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`
  (exec approval tier, description prefixed with the origin, inputSchema
  verbatim) through the manager's `onChanged` (AgentCli re-registers +
  rebuilds the prompt's tiny MCP section). Results map MCP content blocks
  onto ours (text as-is, images as ImageContent, resources/links as text
  placeholders) under a shared 100k-char budget; `isError` throws so the
  loop records an error result; timeouts name `mcp.toolCallTimeoutMs`.
  Wired via `builtinTools(env, mcp:)`; resources/prompts out of scope.
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — model roles (`default`/`smol`/`slow`/`plan`) with
  fallback chains, key rotation (`ApiKeyRing` over `NAME`/`NAME_2`/…), 429
  mid-turn take-over (`FallbackStreamFunction`, never silent). Provider
  streams carry watchdogs (`provider_common.dart`:
  `providerConnectTimeout` 180s for the request, `providerStreamIdleTimeout`
  5min between bytes — overridable via the `providerTimeouts:` config
  section, `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`, published to
  `providerTimeoutsOverride` at startup) so a wedged endpoint errors out — and the resolver
  can fail over — instead of hanging the turn forever. Streaming adapters
  share ONE keep-alive `http.Client` (`sharedProviderHttpClient`) instead of
  a fresh client per call: per-turn TCP churn piled TIME_WAIT sockets into
  connect stalls. Config:
  `roles:`/`modelOverrides:`/`retry:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` (invalid

  the no-fabric fallback); `mailboxPrefix` (the session id, set by the host
  on every session init/switch) namespaces mailboxes so two instances never
  drain each other — ids with `/` are absolute cross-instance addresses

  `agent_message` targets siblings, `main`, a session name, or an
  absolute mailbox; `agent_directory` lists LIVE fabric mailboxes (recent
  activity via the heartbeat hosts touch on their inbox-watch timers) plus
  anything with pending mail — stale mailboxes from finished sessions are
  hidden behind the tool's `all: true` (`.id` markers keep real ids despite
  dir sanitization; `_scheduled`/dot-dirs are not mailboxes).
  `schedule_message` (issue #59): records under `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/`;
  self-addressed records deliver to the host's LIVE mailbox at fire time
  (the address pinned at schedule time goes stale on session switch/restart
  and would strand the reminder) — EXCEPT self-addressed records naming a
  subagent mailbox of this session (`<prefix>/<childId>`, gh-970): those
  deliver as recorded (the address rides the same owner prefix and is as
  stable; re-addressing stole the child's reminder into main), and the
  tool's `senderMailbox` override (host-wired from `activeSubagentId()`)
  makes a subagent's no-`to` schedule default to the CHILD's mailbox, not
  main's — hosts re-arm on every mailbox change
  (CLI `_syncMailboxPrefix`, app `_setMailboxPrefix`) and sweep due records
  on their inbox ticks; `dispose()` cancels only the timer, the files stay.
  gh-1180: a re-addressed SELF record also delivers FROM the live mailbox
  (`from` rewritten alongside `to` in `_deliverDueInner`) — an adopted
  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.
  UI: `/agents` rows show a `mail:N` pending marker (the CLI
  font has no ✉ glyph), the app's AgentsSection shows `✉N`; observe/detail
  views list the pending inbox.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Aggregate + step-summary for bench-programbench.yml (gh-1685).

Runs in the aggregate job AFTER `programbench submit package` (so
_stats/score.json exists — the tool's own ignored-test-filtered map, never
recomputed here) and BEFORE the Tier-0 verify gate:

  1. computes self-reported per-instance cost/calls from the fa session
     logs (bench/fa_usage.py + bench/pricing.json — the #1123 pipeline)
     into _stats/cost.json + _stats/calls.json, the registry's
     {instance_id: value} convention (package preserves sibling _stats
     files; verified against programbench 1.2.5);
  2. renders the markdown summary table (accuracy/cost/calls per task,
     bench-harbor style) on stdout;
  3. fails the run on structural problems: any expected task missing its
     submission.tar.gz / eval.json / packaged score, or a zero-package run
     (a lost shard must never masquerade as a score — the MLS precedent).

Score display: solved = every scored test true (the ✅ convention — a
100-after-rounding instance that isn't solved is NOT solved). The headline
mean is reported over the FULL official set (package divides by `total`,
so a partial run's number is diluted by design; the table is explicit
about it).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def solved_fraction(score_map: dict) -> tuple[int, int, bool]:
    """(passed, total, solved) for one instance's {branch/test: bool} map."""
    total = len(score_map)
    passed = sum(1 for v in score_map.values() if v is True)
    return passed, total, total > 0 and passed == total


def instance_usage(tdir: Path, pricing: dict) -> tuple[float | None, int | None]:
    """(cost_usd | None when unpriced, api_calls) from the shard's copied
    fa session logs; (None, None) when the shard uploaded no sessions."""
    sessions = tdir / "fa-artifacts" / "sessions"
    if not sessions.is_dir():
        return None, None
    usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(str(sessions))
    calls = 0
    for f in sessions.rglob("*.jsonl"):
        for line in f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            if '"role": "assistant"' not in line and '"role":"assistant"' not in line:
                continue
            if '"usage"' in line or '"inputTokens"' in line:
                calls += 1
    model = usage.last_model
    entry = fa_usage.price_entry(pricing, model)
    cost = fa_usage.cost_usd(
        entry,
        usage.input_tokens,
        usage.output_tokens,
        usage.cache_read_tokens,
        usage.cache_write_tokens,
    )
    return cost, calls


def main() -> int:
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    run_dir = Path(a[0])

    def opt(flag: str, default: str = "") -> str:
        return a[a.index(flag) + 1] if flag in a else default

    expected = int(opt("--expected", "0"))
    total = int(opt("--total", "0"))
    mode = opt("--mode", "full")
    run_label = opt("--run-label")
    fa_ref = opt("--fa-ref")
    run_url = opt("--run-url")
    pricing = fa_usage.load_pricing(str(REPO_ROOT / "bench" / "pricing.json"))

    iids = sorted(p.name for p in run_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and not p.name.startswith("_"))
    stats = run_dir / "_stats"
    score_path = stats / "score.json"
    score = json.loads(score_path.read_text()) if score_path.is_file() else {}

    # ── cost/calls: self-reported, from OUR trajectories (guide §3) ────
    costs: dict = {}
    calls: dict = {}
    unpriced = False
    for iid in iids:
        cost, n = instance_usage(run_dir / iid, pricing)
        if n is not None:
            calls[iid] = n
        if cost is not None:
            costs[iid] = round(cost, 4)
        elif n is not None:
            unpriced = True
    stats.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (stats / "cost.json").write_text(json.dumps(costs, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    (stats / "calls.json").write_text(json.dumps(calls, indent=2, sort_keys=True))

    # ── the table ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("## ProgramBench run — fa")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"| | |")
    lines.append(f"|---|---|")
    lines.append(f"| Run | {run_label} |")
    lines.append(f"| fa ref | `{fa_ref[:12]}` |")
    lines.append(f"| Mode | {mode} — {len(iids)} of {total} official instances |")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("| instance | passed | tests | solved | cost (USD) | calls |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for iid in iids:
        m = score.get(iid)
        if isinstance(m, dict):
            p, t, ok = solved_fraction(m)
            solved = "✅" if ok else "—"
            passed_s, tests_s = str(p), str(t)
        else:
            solved, passed_s, tests_s = "⚠️ no score", "-", "-"
        c = costs.get(iid)
        c_s = f"{c:.4f}" if isinstance(c, (int, float)) else ("n/a" if iid in calls else "-")
        lines.append(
            f"| {iid} | {passed_s} | {tests_s} | {solved} | {c_s} | {calls.get(iid, '-')} |"
        )
    solved_n = sum(1 for iid in iids if isinstance(score.get(iid), dict) and solved_fraction(score[iid])[2])
    lines.append("")
    if mode != "full":
        dilution = len(iids) / total if total else 0.0
        lines.append(
            f"**Solved {solved_n}/{len(iids)} attempted.** The package headline "
            f"(`_stats` mean) divides by the full official set ({total}), so it reads "
            f"~{dilution:.1%} of the attempted score — a partial run is a pipeline "
            "proof, not a leaderboard row. Full runs need `tasks: ''` + "
            "`confirm-full-run: true`."
        )
    else:
        lines.append(f"**Solved {solved_n}/{len(iids)} — headline pass@1 over the full official set.**")
    if unpriced:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("⚠️ at least one instance ran an unpriced model — its cost shows `n/a` (bench/pricing.json has no entry); calls are still reported.")
    if run_url:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"Run: {run_url}")

    # ── verdict ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    problems = []
    for iid in iids:
        if not (run_dir / iid / "submission.tar.gz").is_file():
            problems.append(f"{iid}: no submission.tar.gz (solve crashed before packing)")
        if not (run_dir / iid / f"{iid}.eval.json").is_file() and not (run_dir / iid / f"{iid}.eval.log.json").is_file():
            problems.append(f"{iid}: no eval.json (eval never ran or crashed)")
    packaged = [i for i in iids if isinstance(score.get(i), dict)]
    if expected and len(iids) != expected:
        problems.append(f"shard completeness: {len(iids)} task dirs present, expected {expected} — a shard lost work")
    if expected and len(packaged) != expected:
        problems.append(f"package completeness: {len(packaged)}/{expected} instances scored in _stats/score.json")
    if problems:
        print("\n".join(lines))
        print("\n## ❌ Verdict — structural problems\n")
        for p in problems:
            print(f"- {p}")
        return 1
    print("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"\n## ✅ Verdict — all {expected or len(iids)} attempted instances solved, evaluated, and packaged")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shared fa-session token/cost extraction for the bench adapters (issue #1123).

One extraction path for both pipelines (legacy bench/terminal_bench and
Harbor bench/harbor_fa). fa session JSONL assistant records embed
``message.usage = {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, ...}``
(Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart) plus ``message.model``; flat
``inputTokens``-style keys are accepted as a fallback (trajectory export
shape). Only assistant records carry usage — the ``model_request_summary``
ledger records hold request-side sizes only — so summing over records
cannot double-count.

A record whose usage is missing or all-zero (provider omitted it)
contributes a chars/4 estimate tallied separately, so totals stay honest
about what the provider actually reported. The chars/4 rate matches
lib/src/compaction/token_estimation.dart.

Fail-soft by contract (issue #1123): a missing/corrupt session log leaves
zeros + a warning, never a failed trial.

cost derivation reads a pinned price table (bench/pricing.json, $/Mtok,
data not code). A model missing from the table prices as None — the
callers render ``n/a``, never a made-up 0.00.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import math
import sys
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

# Same chars-per-token rate as lib/src/compaction/token_estimation.dart.
_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4


class SessionUsage:
    """Token totals summed over one trial's fa session JSONL records."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.input_tokens = 0
        self.output_tokens = 0
        self.cache_read_tokens = 0
        self.cache_write_tokens = 0
        self.estimated_input_tokens = 0
        self.estimated_output_tokens = 0
        # model id -> per-model tally; "" when the record named no model.
        self.models = {}
        self.warnings = []
        # gh-1643: True when at least one `model_request_summary` never
        # finalized (the run was killed before its assistant message) —
        # the totals cover PARTIAL knowledge (estimated request-side
        # input, no output). Consumers must never read them as complete
        # accounting.
        self.usage_incomplete = False
        # Last model id seen on a finalized request (gh-1643): a dangling
        # request carries no model of its own, so its estimate is
        # attributed to the model the session actually ran on.
        self.last_model = ""

    @property
    def estimated_tokens(self) -> int:
        return self.estimated_input_tokens + self.estimated_output_tokens

    def total_tokens(self) -> int:
        return (
            self.input_tokens
            + self.output_tokens
            + self.cache_read_tokens
            + self.cache_write_tokens
            + self.estimated_tokens
        )


def _per_model(usage: SessionUsage, model: str) -> dict:
    return usage.models.setdefault(
        model,
        {"input": 0, "output": 0, "cacheRead": 0, "cacheWrite": 0, "estimatedOutput": 0},
    )


def _feed_dangling(usage: SessionUsage, known_chars: int) -> None:
    """A `model_request_summary` whose request never finalized (gh-1643).

    The run was killed before its assistant message: the summary's KNOWN
    request-side volume — system prompt + outbound message chars, persisted
    BEFORE the request — counts as estimated input at the shared chars/4
    rate; output is unknown and stays 0. The usage is marked incomplete:
    a request the fold only partially knows is never a silent zero.
    """
    usage.usage_incomplete = True
    est = math.ceil(known_chars / _CHARS_PER_TOKEN)
    if est == 0:
        return
    usage.estimated_input_tokens += est
    model = usage.last_model or ""
    tally = _per_model(usage, model)
    tally["estimatedInput"] = tally.get("estimatedInput", 0) + est


def _request_known_chars(data) -> int:
    """Known request-side chars of one `model_request_summary` record.

    `systemPromptChars` + Σ per-message `chars` — the same basis the Dart
    fold's dangling-request fallback uses (gh-1073's ledger cap preserves
    both, so the estimate survives the newest-tail capping).
    """
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return 0
    total = 0
    system = data.get("systemPromptChars")
    if isinstance(system, int) and not isinstance(system, bool):
        total += system
    messages = data.get("messages")
    if isinstance(messages, list):
        for message in messages:
            if isinstance(message, dict):
                chars = message.get("chars")
                if isinstance(chars, int) and not isinstance(chars, bool):
                    total += chars
    return total


def _content_chars(content) -> int:
    """Char volume of an assistant message's content blocks.

    Estimate basis for records whose usage the provider omitted — tallied
    as ESTIMATED OUTPUT (the content is the response side of the request).
    """
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return len(content)
    if not isinstance(content, list):
        return 0
    n = 0
    for block in content:
        if not isinstance(block, dict):
            continue
        kind = block.get("type")
        if kind == "text":
            n += len(block.get("text") or "")
        elif kind == "thinking":
            n += len(block.get("thinking") or "")
        elif kind == "toolCall":
            args = block.get("arguments")
            if args is not None:
                n += len(args if isinstance(args, str) else json.dumps(args))
    return n


def _feed(usage: SessionUsage, obj) -> None:
    message = obj.get("message") if isinstance(obj, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
        return
    model = message.get("model") or ""
    if model:
        usage.last_model = model
    usage_or_flat = message.get("usage")
    if not isinstance(usage_or_flat, dict):
        # Flat trajectory-export shape fallback.
        usage_or_flat = {
            "input": message.get("inputTokens"),
            "output": message.get("outputTokens"),
            "cacheRead": message.get("cacheReadTokens"),
            "cacheWrite": message.get("cacheWriteTokens"),
        }

    def num(key) -> int:
        value = usage_or_flat.get(key)
        # Some providers emit floats (or strings) for token counts; a
        # silent 0 here would reroute a real report into the estimate path.
        if isinstance(value, bool):
            return 0
        if isinstance(value, int):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, float):
            # Fractional token counts round UP: under-counting spend is
            # the worse failure, and ceil matches the estimate path.
            return int(value) if value.is_integer() else math.ceil(value)
        return 0

    inp, out = num("input"), num("output")
    cr, cw = num("cacheRead"), num("cacheWrite")
    if inp == 0 and out == 0 and cr == 0 and cw == 0:
        # Provider omitted usage: contribute a chars/4 estimate, marked as such.
        reported = [
            usage_or_flat.get(key)
            for key in ("input", "output", "cacheRead", "cacheWrite")
        ]
        if reported and not any(
            isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) for v in reported
        ):
            # The record LOOKS like it carries usage but nothing parsed —
            # say so instead of quietly estimating real spend away.
            usage.warnings.append(
                "malformed usage record (no numeric token fields); "
                "estimated from content chars/4"
            )
        est = math.ceil(_content_chars(message.get("content")) / _CHARS_PER_TOKEN)
        usage.estimated_output_tokens += est
        _per_model(usage, model)["estimatedOutput"] += est
        return
    usage.input_tokens += inp
    usage.output_tokens += out
    usage.cache_read_tokens += cr
    usage.cache_write_tokens += cw
    tally = _per_model(usage, model)
    tally["input"] += inp
    tally["output"] += out
    tally["cacheRead"] += cr
    tally["cacheWrite"] += cw


def extract_from_text(text: str, usage: SessionUsage = None) -> SessionUsage:
    """Sum usage over concatenated JSONL text (container exec / single file).

    gh-1643: request-side records fold too. A `model_request_summary` whose
    request never produced a finalized assistant message — flushed by a
    later summary, a segment marker, a session header, or the end of the
    text — contributes its KNOWN request-side volume as estimated input and
    sets `usage_incomplete`. Finalized requests never double-count: the
    assistant message's usage supersedes its summary.
    """
    usage = usage if usage is not None else SessionUsage()
    pending_chars = None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if (
            '"usage"' not in line
            and '"inputTokens"' not in line
            and '"model_request_summary"' not in line
            and '"usage_segment_start"' not in line
        ):
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue  # corrupt line contributes nothing (fail-soft)
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            continue
        custom_type = obj.get("customType")
        if custom_type == "model_request_summary":
            if pending_chars is not None:
                # The previous request never finalized — count it now.
                _feed_dangling(usage, pending_chars)
            pending_chars = _request_known_chars(obj.get("data"))
            continue
        if custom_type == "usage_segment_start":
            if pending_chars is not None:
                _feed_dangling(usage, pending_chars)
                pending_chars = None
            continue
        if obj.get("type") == "session":
            # A new chain header: anything pending belongs to the previous
            # chain (replay/takeover file pairs) — it never finalized.
            if pending_chars is not None:
                _feed_dangling(usage, pending_chars)
                pending_chars = None
            continue
        _feed(usage, obj)
        message = obj.get("message")
        if isinstance(message, dict) and message.get("role") == "assistant":
            # The request finalized: its summary is superseded by the
            # message usage — never double-count.
            pending_chars = None
    if pending_chars is not None:
        _feed_dangling(usage, pending_chars)
    return usage


def extract_from_dir(sessions_dir, usage: SessionUsage = None) -> SessionUsage:
    """Sum usage over every *.jsonl under the trial's fah-sessions dir.
    rglob covers retries (multiple sessions per trial) and subagent
    sessions — all of it is the trial's real spend (issue #1123 E1/E2).
    """
    usage = usage if usage is not None else SessionUsage()
    sessions_dir = Path(sessions_dir)
    if not sessions_dir.is_dir():
        usage.warnings.append(f"session dir missing: {sessions_dir}")
        return usage
    for path in sorted(sessions_dir.rglob("*.jsonl")):
        try:
            extract_from_text(path.read_text(errors="replace"), usage)
        except OSError as exc:
            usage.warnings.append(f"unreadable session log {path}: {exc}")
    return usage


def extract_session_archive(tar_bytes: bytes, dest) -> int:
    """Unpack a docker get_archive tarball of the container's session root
    into the trial's host agent-logs dir (issue #1339 AC4). Returns the
    extracted file count.

    The archive originates from a container path the model's own bash tool
    can write, so the data filter's traversal rules are re-asserted
    manually on EVERY interpreter BEFORE anything is extracted — a guard
    that vanishes on a TypeError fallback is not a guard (PR #1351
    review): only regular files and directories, no absolute paths, no
    `..` members, nothing resolving outside dest. Violations fail loud;
    the tarfile data filter is then applied where the interpreter has it.
    """
    root = Path(dest).resolve()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(tar_bytes)) as tar:
        members = tar.getmembers()
        for member in members:
            if not (member.isfile() or member.isdir()):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"non-regular member in session archive: {member.name!r}"
                )
            if member.name.startswith("/") or ".." in PurePosixPath(member.name).parts:
                raise ValueError(f"unsafe path in session archive: {member.name!r}")
            if not (root / member.name).resolve().is_relative_to(root):
                raise ValueError(f"path escapes the trial dir: {member.name!r}")
        try:
            tar.extractall(dest, members=members, filter="data")
        except TypeError:  # pre-backport interpreter: no filter kwarg
            print(
                "[fa_agent] warning: this Python lacks the tarfile data "
                "filter; extracting the manually screened session archive "
                "without it",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            tar.extractall(dest, members=members)
        return sum(1 for member in members if member.isfile())


def load_pricing(path) -> dict:
    """Load the pinned $/Mtok table (bench/pricing.json shape). Missing → {}."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            data = json.load(handle)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}
    table = data.get("usd_per_mtok") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    return table if isinstance(table, dict) else {}


def price_entry(pricing: dict, model) -> dict | None:
    """Pricing entry for a model id (exact, then case-insensitive); None = unpriced."""
    if not model:
        return None
    if model in pricing:
        return pricing[model]
    lowered = str(model).lower()
    for key, entry in pricing.items():
        if key.lower() == lowered:
            return entry
    return None


def cost_usd(
    entry: dict | None,
    input_tokens: int,
    output_tokens: int,
    cache_read_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_write_tokens: int = 0,
) -> float | None:
    """USD for a token split under one pricing entry; None when unpriced (E3)."""
    if entry is None:
        return None

    def rate(key) -> float:
        value = entry.get(key)
        # A rate the table omits prices at 0 only because the table pins the
        # rest; an absent MODEL is handled by price_entry → None (n/a).
        return float(value) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else 0.0

    return (
        input_tokens * rate("input")
        + output_tokens * rate("output")
        + cache_read_tokens * rate("cache_read")
        + cache_write_tokens * rate("cache_write")
    ) / 1e6

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UTs for run_shard.py's eval step (gh-1816).

Root cause under test: `programbench eval` defaults to DOCKER_CPUS=10 and
creates every eval container with `docker run --cpus 10`; GH hosted runners
expose 4 CPUs to the docker daemon, which rejects the container
("range of CPUs is from 0.01 to 4.00"), so eval died per instance with
`ERROR: RuntimeError` and never wrote eval.json. The shard driver must cap
programbench at the daemon's own CPU count (PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS).

Evidence gap under test: eval_all() printed only `proc.stdout[-4000:]` and
dropped stderr entirely — the diagnosing traceback (logging writes stderr)
never reached the CI log. The full output must tee into the run dir and the
failure path must surface stderr.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/programbench
"""
import contextlib
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import run_shard


@contextlib.contextmanager
def tempfile_dir():
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pbench-evaltest-")
    try:
        yield Path(d)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)


def make_shard(tmp: Path) -> run_shard.Shard:
    """A Shard with __init__'s docker/env plumbing bypassed."""
    shard = run_shard.Shard.__new__(run_shard.Shard)
    shard.run_dir = tmp
    shard.eval_workers = 1
    return shard


class FakeProc:
    def __init__(self, stdout: str = "", stderr: str = "", returncode: int = 0):
        self.stdout = stdout
        self.stderr = stderr
        self.returncode = returncode


class EvalDockerCpusTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """gh-1816: eval must run with PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS <= daemon NCPU."""

    def setUp(self):
        self._saved = os.environ.get("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS")
        os.environ.pop("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS", None)
        self.calls: list[tuple[list[str], dict]] = []

    def tearDown(self):
        if self._saved is None:
            os.environ.pop("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS", None)
        else:
            os.environ["PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS"] = self._saved

    def patch_run(self, procs):
        real_run = run_shard.run

        def fake_run(cmd, **kw):
            self.calls.append((list(cmd), kw))
            if cmd[:2] == ["docker", "info"]:
                return procs["info"]
            return procs["eval"]

        run_shard.run = fake_run
        self.addCleanup(setattr, run_shard, "run", real_run)

    def test_eval_caps_cpus_at_daemon_ncpu(self):
        self.patch_run({
            "info": FakeProc(stdout="4\n"),
            "eval": FakeProc(stdout="summary", returncode=0),
        })
        with tempfile_dir() as tmp:
            shard = make_shard(tmp)
            self.assertTrue(shard.eval_all())
        eval_calls = [c for c in self.calls if c[0][0] == "programbench"]
        self.assertEqual(len(eval_calls), 1)
        env = eval_calls[0][1].get("env") or {}
        self.assertEqual(
            env.get("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS"), "4",
            "eval must pass PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS = docker daemon NCPU",
        )

    def test_eval_respects_preset_cpus_env(self):
        os.environ["PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS"] = "2"
        self.patch_run({
            "info": FakeProc(stdout="4\n"),
            "eval": FakeProc(stdout="", returncode=0),
        })
        with tempfile_dir() as tmp:
            shard = make_shard(tmp)
            self.assertTrue(shard.eval_all())
        eval_calls = [c for c in self.calls if c[0][0] == "programbench"]
        env = eval_calls[0][1].get("env") or {}
        self.assertEqual(env.get("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS"), "2")

    def test_ncpu_falls_back_to_cpu_count_on_daemon_error(self):
        self.patch_run({
            "info": FakeProc(stderr="cannot connect", returncode=1),
            "eval": FakeProc(stdout="", returncode=0),
        })
        self.assertEqual(run_shard.docker_ncpu(), max(1, os.cpu_count() or 1))

    def test_ncpu_floors_garbage_output_at_one(self):
        self.patch_run({
            "info": FakeProc(stdout="not-a-number\n"),
            "eval": FakeProc(stdout="", returncode=0),
        })
        self.assertGreaterEqual(run_shard.docker_ncpu(), 1)


class EvalOutputTeeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """gh-1816 evidence gap: full eval stdout+stderr must survive into the
    run dir (rides the shard artifact) and stderr must surface on failure."""

    def setUp(self):
        self._saved = os.environ.get("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS")
        os.environ["PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS"] = "4"

    def tearDown(self):
        if self._saved is None:
            os.environ.pop("PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS", None)
        else:
            os.environ["PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS"] = self._saved

    def patch_run(self, proc):
        real_run = run_shard.run
        run_shard.run = lambda cmd, **kw: proc
        self.addCleanup(setattr, run_shard, "run", real_run)

    def test_failure_teees_full_output_and_surfaces_stderr(self):
        big_out = "x" * 20000
        trace = "RuntimeError: Failed to start container: range of CPUs ...\n"
        self.patch_run(FakeProc(stdout=big_out, stderr=trace, returncode=1))
        captured = []
        real_write = sys.stdout.write
        sys.stdout.write = lambda s: captured.append(s)
        try:
            with tempfile_dir() as tmp:
                shard = make_shard(tmp)
                self.assertFalse(shard.eval_all())
                tee_out = (tmp / "eval-stdout.log").read_text()
                tee_err = (tmp / "eval-stderr.log").read_text()
        finally:
            sys.stdout.write = real_write
        self.assertEqual(tee_out, big_out, "full stdout must tee into the run dir")
        self.assertEqual(tee_err, trace, "full stderr must tee into the run dir")
        printed = "".join(captured)
        self.assertIn("Failed to start container", printed,
                      "failure path must print the stderr tail (the traceback)")

    def test_success_also_teees_output(self):
        self.patch_run(FakeProc(stdout="all good", stderr="", returncode=0))
        with tempfile_dir() as tmp:
            shard = make_shard(tmp)
            self.assertTrue(shard.eval_all())
            self.assertEqual((tmp / "eval-stdout.log").read_text(), "all good")
            self.assertEqual((tmp / "eval-stderr.log").read_text(), "")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# maintainer TODO fields), _stats/score.json (the ignored-test-
      # filtered per-instance map), the checklist README, and splits each
      # heavy eval log. Accepts a partial run (verified against 1.2.5).
      - name: Package submission
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          programbench submit package "pbench-run/$RUN_ID"

      # Accuracy/cost/calls table (bench-harbor style) + the structural
      # verdict: every expected instance packed, evaluated, and scored.
      # Writes _stats/cost.json + _stats/calls.json (self-reported, from
      # the fa session logs) — package preserves sibling _stats files
      # (verified against 1.2.5).
      - name: Summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          TOTAL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.total }}
          MODE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.mode }}
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python bench/programbench/summary.py "pbench-run/$RUN_ID" \
            --expected "$EXPECTED" --total "$TOTAL" --mode "$MODE" \
            --run-label "$BENCH_RUN_LABEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            | tee "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # AC2's gate: the packaged folder must pass the registry's own
      # Tier-0 check (headline recomputation from the artifacts — instant,
      # no docker). A submission that cannot pass verify never leaves CI.
      - name: Verify submission (Tier-0)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          programbench submit verify "pbench-run/$RUN_ID"

      # The one-step handoff artifact: exactly the folder docs/bench.md
      # tells a maintainer to publish + PR to ProgramBench/submissions.
      - name: Upload submission folder
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: programbench-submission
          path: pbench-run/
          # gh-182 review: the ledger links this artifact as the run's
          # analysis surface (trajectories, eval logs, _stats) — it must
          # outlive the default 90-day retention window, or README and
          # fa1.dev accumulate dead links.
          retention-days: 365

tasks immediately (exit 2 — never retried inline: no trial starts into a
dead quota window; rerun the dispatch to resume, remaining tasks are
marked skipped). Only a zero-trial startup crash (docker pull / airgap /
resolve transient) gets the gh-1658-style single inline retry; a failure
with trials is a real result and never retried. The setup resolve step
preflights the provider secret before any spend.

### Results

1. **Job summary** — the accuracy/cost/calls table per instance
   (`bench/programbench/summary.py`), the solved ✅ column, and the
   structural verdict (every attempted instance packed, evaluated, and
   scored — a lost shard fails the run, never a silent score). A partial
   run's headline is dilution-labeled in the table: `submit package`
   divides by the full official set.
2. **Artifacts** — per-shard run dirs (`pbench-shard-*`) and
   `programbench-submission`: the packaged, Tier-0-verified folder with
   `submission.yaml`, `_stats/score.json` (the tool's ignored-test-
   filtered map — never recomputed harness-side), self-reported
   `_stats/cost.json` + `_stats/calls.json` computed from the fa session
   logs via `bench/fa_usage.py` + `bench/pricing.json`, per-instance
   `submission.tar.gz` + `*.eval.json` + `*.traj.json`.
3. **Verdict gate** — `programbench submit verify` (Tier-0) must pass in
   CI; a submission that cannot pass the registry's own check never
   leaves the run.

The workflow stops at the verified artifact — publishing is a maintainer
decision. Per the official submission guide:

- [金融晨报智能体设计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/official-financial-morning-report-agent.md): 介绍官方金融晨报监控智能体的定时调度、双插件分工和无人值守运行方式，并提供起始配置、运行成本估算与搭建指南。
- [港股 IPO 扫描智能体设计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/official-hk-ipo-scan-agent.md): 介绍官方港股 IPO 扫描智能体的定时监控架构、不可信招股书处理规则和 A/H 对标数据设计，并提供起始配置、运行成本估算与搭建指南。

- [金融监管处罚日报智能体设计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/regulatory-daily-report-agent.md): 用托管智能体每天定时下载监管机构行政处罚公示，结构化保存处罚记录并生成日报草稿，覆盖职责分工、技能封装、定时任务、按域代理与人工审核流程。

- [玩家游戏顾问智能体设计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/game-advisor-agent.md): 用托管智能体构建游戏内置顾问：游戏知识与玩家状态两类数据的划分、防剧透策略、系统提示词设计，以及从最小版本到接入真实游戏数据的完整路径。
- [出海社群运营智能体设计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/discord-community-ops-agent.md): 使用 Kimi 托管智能体整理 Discord 社区反馈、生成简报和回复草稿，基于历史问答，并在人工审核后批量发送消息。
- [AI 小游戏研运智能体设计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/mini-game-studio.md): 使用四个定时触发的托管智能体搭建 AI 小游戏研运流程：热点选题、游戏制作、演示视频录制和 Discord 发布，包含三道人工审核。部署由企业自建服务完成。附完整起始配置、运行成本估算与搭建步骤。
- [常见问题](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/faq.md): 托管智能体常见问题：资源概念与区别、版本与并发、会话运行与故障、文件与记忆库、控制台能力边界。
- [更新日志](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/hosted-agents/changelog.md): 托管智能体 API 的调用方可见变更记录：新增能力、行为变更与契约声明更新。
- [API 概述](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/overview.md): 查看 Kimi API 的服务地址、认证方式、请求格式、兼容性和主要接口入口。
- [模型参数参考](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/models-overview.md): 对比 Kimi 各模型系列在 Chat Completions API 中的默认参数、可调范围与使用约束。
- [常见错误码说明](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/errors.md): 查询 Kimi API 的 HTTP 状态码、错误类型、常见原因和对应的排查处理方法。
- [Chat Completions API](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/chat.md): 创建对话补全：向 Kimi 模型发送消息并获取回复，支持流式输出、工具调用与视觉输入。
- [Responses API](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/responses.md): 创建一次模型响应。传入文本或图片，生成文本或 JSON 输出；也可以让模型调用你定义的函数工具，或使用服务端执行的联网搜索。
- [Messages API](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/messages.md): 以 Anthropic Messages API 兼容的格式调用 Kimi 模型，支持流式输出、工具调用、图片输入、思考与结构化输出。
- [列出模型](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/list-models.md): 列出当前可用的模型及其 ID。
- [计算 Token](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/estimate.md): 在发送请求前估算输入内容的 Token 数量。
- [查询余额](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/balance.md): 查询当前账户的可用余额。
- [校验请求签名](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/signatures-verify.md): 校验 Kimi API 返回的请求签名，证明请求确实由 Kimi API 处理且请求的是指定模型，而非被转发到其他服务。
- [联网搜索 Basic](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/tools-search.md): 通过 /v1/tools/search 接口发起网页搜索，返回结构化搜索结果。
- [联网搜索 Pro](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/tools-search-pro.md): 通过 /v1/tools/search_pro 接口发起网页搜索，支持站点与时间范围约束，并返回结构化正文片段。
- [网页抓取](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/tools-fetch.md): 通过 /v1/tools/fetch 接口抓取指定 URL 的网页内容，返回页面标题与 Markdown 格式正文。
- [上传文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/files-upload.md): 上传文件用于文本内容抽取、图片理解或视频理解，支持 pdf、doc、txt 等文本类格式。
- [列出文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/files-list.md): 列出当前账户已上传的文件。
- [获取文件信息](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/files-retrieve.md): 获取指定文件的元信息。
- [删除文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/files-delete.md): 删除指定的已上传文件。
- [获取文件内容](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/files-content.md): 获取以 file-extract 用途上传的文件的提取内容，返回 Markdown 格式文本。
- [创建批处理任务](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/batch-create.md): 创建批处理任务，以更低价格异步批量处理请求。
- [列出批处理任务](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/batch-list.md): 列出当前账户的批处理任务。
- [获取批处理任务详情](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/batch-retrieve.md): 获取指定批处理任务的详情与进度。
- [取消批处理任务](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/batch-cancel.md): 取消一个进行中的批处理任务。
- [列出智能体](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/智能体/列出智能体.md): 返回调用方的智能体，默认最新在前，除非 `order` 为 `created_at`。已归档的智能体不会出现在列表中。
- [创建智能体](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/智能体/创建智能体.md): 创建智能体及其首个不可变版本（`"1"`）。
- [获取智能体](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/智能体/获取智能体.md): 返回单个智能体及其最新版本。已归档的智能体仍可读取。
- [更新智能体](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/智能体/更新智能体.md): 修改请求体中提供的字段，并创建一个新的不可变智能体版本。
- [归档智能体](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/智能体/归档智能体.md): 归档智能体。已归档的智能体仍可读取，但不能更新，也不能用于开启新会话。已有会话不受影响。
- [列出智能体版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/智能体/列出智能体版本.md): 返回智能体的不可变版本，最新在前。每一项都是该版本捕获的完整配置。
- [列出产物](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/产物/列出产物.md): 列出调用方可见的产物，最近交付的在前。每个条目为该产物的最新版本。用 `session_id` 筛选单个会话的产物。
- [获取产物](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/产物/获取产物.md): 返回单个产物的元数据。未指定 `version` 时返回最新版本，指定时返回该确切版本。
- [删除产物](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/产物/删除产物.md): 永久删除一个产物及其全部版本。已上报该产物的事件不会撤回。
- [下载产物内容](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/产物/下载产物内容.md): 下载产物内容。未指定 `version` 时下载最新版本。
- [列出产物版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/产物/列出产物版本.md): 列出一个产物的全部版本，最新在前。每个条目为该版本的完整产物。
- [列出环境](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/环境/列出环境.md): 返回调用方的环境，最新在前。除非 `include_archived` 为 true，否则不包含已归档的环境。
- [创建环境](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/环境/创建环境.md): 创建一个环境，将其配置冻结为不可变版本 `"1"`，并开始构建。
- [获取环境](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/环境/获取环境.md): 返回单个环境，包括其最新版本的构建状态。已归档的环境仍可读取。
- [删除环境](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/环境/删除环境.md): 永久删除一个已归档的环境及其全部版本。
- [更新环境](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/环境/更新环境.md): 仅修改请求体中出现的字段。`null` 值会被拒绝（400 `invalid_parameter_error`），传入空对象或空数组可清空对应集合。
- [归档环境](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/环境/归档环境.md): 归档一个环境。已归档的环境拒绝更新，也不能承载新会话。现有会话不受影响。
- [列出工作行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/列出工作行.md): 按最新在前列出环境的工作行。终态行作为审计轨迹保留，除非用 `status` 筛选，否则一并返回。
- [轮询认领工作行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/轮询认领工作行.md): 为调用方认领环境中最早的待处理工作行。返回的工作行处于租约状态：通过 ack 确认、心跳续租和 stop 释放，期间始终携带 poll 返回的 `generation`。`block_ms` 大于零时，调用将长轮询直到有工作到达或预算耗尽（届时返回空响应）。成功的 poll 即一次认领：不要对它做幂等重试。
- [工作队列统计](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/工作队列统计.md): 返回该环境的队列统计（按活跃行实时计算）：`depth` 为待认领行数，`claimed` 为租约中行数，`workers` 为持有租约的不同 worker 数，`oldest_queued_at` 为最老待认领行的入队时间（无待认领行时缺省）。
- [获取工作行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/获取工作行.md): 按 ID 返回一个工作行。任意生命周期状态的行均可返回，包括保留作审计的终态行。
- [确认收到投递的工作行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/确认收到投递的工作行.md): 确认收到已投递的工作行（`queued` → `starting`），记录 `acknowledged_at`——不在固定 ack 窗口（5000ms，由后台 sweeper 回收）内确认，工作行将被退回队列。投递后须立即 Ack，慢 executor 启动须在 Ack 之后。过期 token 将被拒绝并返回 412 `failed_precondition_error`。
- [心跳续租工作行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/心跳续租工作行.md): 续租调用方持有的已认领工作行。（`id`、`worker_id`、`generation`）三元组必须与该行的当前状态一致：token 过期意味着工作行已被回收并可能被其他 worker 重新认领，调用将失败并返回 412 `failed_precondition_error`，其中携带当前 generation——请重新轮询以重同步。
- [停止或完成工作行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/工作队列/停止或完成工作行.md): 不传 `final_status` 时请求优雅停止：工作行进入 `stopping`，worker 在下次心跳中收到该状态，取消在飞工具，在续租期间完成结果回写，再提交 `final_status: completed`。确认时若会话仍忙碌则取消会话，并将工作行释放为 `completed`。
- [列出文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/文件/列出文件.md): 列出已上传的文件。不带 `kimi-api-version` 请求头的请求列出整个组织的文件列表；`2026-09-01-beta` 请求列出项目下的文件。不带 `page_size` 时返回完整列表。通过 `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/resources` 将文件挂载到会话。
- [上传文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/文件/上传文件.md): 以 multipart 表单数据上传一个文件，并返回其文件记录。
- [获取文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/文件/获取文件.md): 返回单个文件的元数据。
- [删除文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/文件/删除文件.md): 删除一个文件，并释放其名称供后续上传使用。`batch` 文件只能由上传它的用户删除，否则返回 403。
- [获取文件内容](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/文件/获取文件内容.md): 返回文件按其处理用途可用的内容。
- [列出记忆库](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/列出记忆库.md): 返回调用方的记忆库，最新在前。除非 `include_archived` 为 true，否则不包含已归档的记忆库。
- [创建记忆库](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/创建记忆库.md): 创建项目作用域的记忆库。
- [获取记忆库](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/获取记忆库.md): 返回单个记忆库的元数据。已归档的记忆库仍可读取。
- [删除记忆库](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/删除记忆库.md): 永久删除已归档的记忆库及其全部文件和版本历史。
- [更新记忆库](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/更新记忆库.md): 重命名记忆库或修改其描述。请求体中未出现的字段保持当前值。
- [归档记忆库](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/归档记忆库.md): 归档一个记忆库。归档不可撤销。
- [列出记忆](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/列出记忆.md): 返回记忆库当前的文件，最新在前，不含文件内容。已删除的文件不在其中。已归档的记忆库仍可读取。
- [创建记忆](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/创建记忆.md): 在记忆库中创建一个文件，并记录为第一个版本。
- [获取记忆](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/获取记忆.md): 返回单个文件的元数据和当前的 base64 编码内容。已删除的文件返回 404。已归档的记忆库仍可读取。
- [删除记忆](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/删除记忆.md): 删除文件并记录一个 `deleted` 版本。文件的版本历史仍可读取。对已删除的文件再次删除返回 404。
- [更新记忆](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/更新记忆.md): 修改文件的路径、内容或两者，并把更改记录为新版本。
- [列出记忆版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/列出记忆版本.md): 返回文件的版本历史，仅含元数据。默认最旧在前，`order` 为 `desc` 时最新在前。已删除文件的版本仍可列出。
- [获取记忆版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/获取记忆版本.md): 返回单个版本的元数据及其历史内容的 base64 编码。`deleted` 版本以及已删除正文的版本不返回内容。
- [删除记忆版本正文](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/删除记忆版本正文.md): 永久删除一个历史版本的正文，仅保留其元数据。已删除的正文无法恢复。
- [获取梦境策略](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/获取梦境策略.md): 返回单个记忆库的梦境策略。
- [更新梦境策略](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/记忆库/更新梦境策略.md): 整体替换单个记忆库的梦境策略。
- [列出插件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/列出插件.md): 返回可用于智能体配置的已上架插件，按 ID 升序排列。`query` 对名称、描述和关键词做大小写不敏感匹配。
- [创建插件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/创建插件.md): 通过 `.zip` 插件包上传发布一个项目自有的插件及其第一个版本。
- [校验插件包](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/校验插件包.md): 校验一个插件包并返回全部结论，不产生任何副作用。
- [获取插件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/获取插件.md): 返回单个已上架插件，包括其捆绑的 MCP 服务器与技能。未上架的插件返回 404。
- [归档插件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/归档插件.md): 归档一个项目自有的插件。
- [列出插件版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/列出插件版本.md): 返回该插件已发布的版本，语义版本最新的在前。已归档插件的版本不再可读。
- [创建插件版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/创建插件版本.md): 通过 `.zip` 插件包上传为项目自有插件发布一个新的不可变版本。
- [获取插件版本内容](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/插件/获取插件版本内容.md): 下载项目自有插件指定确切发布版本的插件包归档。响应始终为 `application/zip`，字节与提交时的归档一致。`official` 插件不提供插件包下载，返回 400 `failed_precondition_error`。已归档的插件返回 404。
- [列出会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出会话.md): 返回调用方的会话，最近更新的排在最前，除非 `order` 另有指定。列表项省略 `resources` 绑定。请使用 `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` 获取。
- [创建会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/创建会话.md): 创建运行选定智能体版本的会话，初始状态为 `idle`。
- [获取会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/获取会话.md): 返回单个会话，包含其资源绑定和协调者的智能体快照（含系统提示词）。
- [删除会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/删除会话.md): 永久删除一个已归档的会话及其资源绑定。
- [更新会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/更新会话.md): 修改会话的标题或智能体覆盖配置。仅 `title` 与 `agent_overrides` 可修改，请求体中未出现的字段保持原值。
- [归档会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/归档会话.md): 归档会话：将其终止并取消其线程。运行中的会话无法归档（400 `failed_precondition_error`），正在停止的会话返回 409 `conflict_error`。先发送 `user.interrupt` 事件，等待会话空闲后再归档。已归档的会话拒绝更新和新事件，但仍可读取。
- [继续会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/继续会话.md): 恢复当前空闲且已中断的会话，不需要请求体。正在停止或已终止的会话返回 409 `conflict_error`。未中断的会话保持不变。延迟或重试的请求可能恢复后来的一次停止。等待返回的控制版本上 `continue_pending` 变为 false；更新的控制版本会取代本次请求。保留已有排队输入，本操作不添加消息。恢复 self-hosted 会话时，若 worker 租约已释放，则重新入队工作行。
- [列出会话事件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出会话事件.md): 分页返回会话的事件历史，最旧的在前——即协调者线程的事件。仅供流式传输的 `agent.delta` 事件从不出现在历史中。
- [向会话发送事件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/向会话发送事件.md): 接收用户事件作为会话输入，返回 202。接受不代表已消费：待处理输入出现在「列出待处理事件」接口中，此时尚未作为 `user.message` 出现在事件历史中。
- [列出待处理事件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出待处理事件.md): 按到达顺序返回会话排队中的输入事件。列表不分页。
- [撤回待处理事件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/撤回待处理事件.md): 在投递前移除一个排队中的输入事件。`event_id` 已投递、已撤回或从未排队时，返回 400。
- [流式获取会话事件（SSE）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/流式获取会话事件（sse）.md): 通过 Server-Sent Events 打开会话的实时事件流。
- [列出会话文件系统中的文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出会话文件系统中的文件.md): 列出会话文件系统中一个目录的直接子项：目录在前，随后文件按名称排序。列表不递归。
- [下载会话文件系统中的文件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/下载会话文件系统中的文件.md): 下载会话文件系统中的一个文件。`path` 为必填，取列表结果中的路径。
- [列出会话资源](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出会话资源.md): 返回绑定到会话的资源，每项都带有服务端分配的绑定 `id`。
- [添加会话资源](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/添加会话资源.md): 将一个已上传的文件绑定到会话，并返回该绑定。
- [获取会话资源](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/获取会话资源.md): 返回会话的一个资源绑定。
- [移除会话资源](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/移除会话资源.md): 从会话中移除一个资源绑定。对于文件，工作区中的链接会一并移除。
- [列出会话的线程](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出会话的线程.md): 返回会话的线程：协调者在前，随后按创建顺序列出子线程，每个线程都带有固定的智能体快照。
- [获取会话的线程](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/获取会话的线程.md): 返回会话的一个线程，包含其固定的智能体快照。
- [归档会话的线程](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/归档会话的线程.md): 终止子线程并取消其当前执行，会话正在停止时也允许操作。对协调者返回 400 `failed_precondition_error`，应改为归档会话。
- [列出线程事件](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/列出线程事件.md): 分页返回单个线程的事件历史，最旧的在前。会话级接口返回协调者线程的历史。`order` 取 `*_desc` 时最新在前，此时 `page_token` 继续向更早的事件翻页。
- [流式获取线程事件（SSE）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/会话/流式获取线程事件（sse）.md): 通过 Server-Sent Events 订阅一个线程的实时公开事件流。帧格式、增量投递与游标语义均与会话事件流相同。
- [列出技能](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/列出技能.md): 返回调用方项目的技能与已启用的官方技能，按创建时间升序排列。已归档的技能不会列出。
- [创建技能](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/创建技能.md): 通过 `.zip` 或 `.skill` 包上传创建项目拥有的技能及其第一个不可变版本。
- [获取技能](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/获取技能.md): 返回单个技能。已归档的技能返回 404。
- [删除技能](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/删除技能.md): 删除一个项目拥有的技能——等同于 `POST /v1/skills/{id}/archive`。
- [归档技能](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/归档技能.md): 归档一个项目拥有的技能。`DELETE /v1/skills/{id}` 是该操作的别名。
- [列出技能版本](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/列出技能版本.md): 返回技能的不可变版本，最新在前。已归档技能的版本仍可列出。
- [获取技能版本内容](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/技能/获取技能版本内容.md): 下载指定确切版本的原始 SKILL.md 指令（`version` 必须是数字版本号，不能是 `latest`）。响应始终为 `text/markdown`。已归档的技能返回 404。
- [列出触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/列出触发器.md): 返回调用方的触发器，最新在前。不设置 `status` 时不包含已归档的触发器。`policy_type` 按策略类型筛选，`agent_id` 按所属 Agent 筛选。
- [创建触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/创建触发器.md): 创建一个处于活跃状态的触发器，为智能体启动会话。
- [获取触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/获取触发器.md): 返回单个触发器。cron 策略处于活跃状态时包含即将到来的运行时间。
- [更新触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/更新触发器.md): 仅修改请求体中出现的字段。传入空对象或空数组可清空集合，`null` 值会被拒绝（400 `invalid_parameter_error`）。状态变更通过暂停、恢复与归档操作进行。
- [归档触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/归档触发器.md): 永久归档触发器：归档后不再触发，`reuse_session` 绑定被释放，运行记录保留。
- [暂停触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/暂停触发器.md): 停止计划运行。暂停期间触发器不参与调度，原本会触发的时刻不产生运行记录。进行中的运行不受影响，仍可手动运行。暂停已暂停的触发器为空操作。平台管理的触发器（`origin_type` 已设置）与已归档的触发器会被拒绝，返回 400 `failed_precondition_error`。
- [运行触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/运行触发器.md): 立即触发一次触发器——包括已暂停的触发器——并同步执行，返回终态的触发器运行记录（`completed`、`failed` 或 `skipped`）。
- [列出触发器运行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/列出触发器运行.md): 返回一个触发器的运行记录，最新在前。用 `has_error` 可只筛出失败的运行。
- [获取触发器运行](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/获取触发器运行.md): 返回单次触发器运行。属于其他触发器的运行返回 404。
- [恢复触发器](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/触发器/恢复触发器.md): 恢复已暂停触发器的计划运行。调度从当前时刻重新开始——暂停期间错过的运行不会补跑。恢复活跃的触发器为空操作。平台管理的触发器（`origin_type` 已设置）与已归档的触发器会被拒绝，返回 400 `failed_precondition_error`。
- [列出凭据库（Vault）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/列出凭据库（vault）.md): 返回调用方的凭据库（Vault），最新者在前。除非 `include_archived` 为 true，否则不包含已归档的凭据库。
- [创建凭据库（Vault）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/创建凭据库（vault）.md): 创建一个凭据库（Vault），用于将凭据分组以绑定到会话。
- [检查凭据覆盖情况](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/检查凭据覆盖情况.md): 按请求顺序，报告每个请求的 MCP 服务器 URL 分别在哪些凭据库（Vault）中持有活跃凭据。
- [获取凭据库（Vault）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/获取凭据库（vault）.md): 返回一个凭据库（Vault）的元数据。已归档的凭据库（Vault）仍可读取。
- [删除凭据库（Vault）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/删除凭据库（vault）.md): 永久删除一个已归档的凭据库（Vault）及其全部凭据。
- [更新凭据库（Vault）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/更新凭据库（vault）.md): 重命名凭据库（Vault）或替换其元数据。请求体中未出现的字段保持当前值。
- [归档凭据库（Vault）](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/归档凭据库（vault）.md): 归档凭据库（Vault）及其全部活跃凭据，并清除其秘密值。已归档的凭据不再对会话可用。
- [列出凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/列出凭据.md): 返回凭据库（Vault）中的凭据，最新者在前，秘密值不返回。除非 `include_archived` 为 true，否则不包含已归档的凭据。
- [创建凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/创建凭据.md): 在凭据库（Vault）中存储一条凭据。秘密值为只写：仅在请求中接受，静态加密存储，且在任何响应中都不返回。
- [批量创建凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/批量创建凭据.md): 以原子方式创建 1–20 条凭据：任一条目校验失败则全部不创建。
- [获取凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/获取凭据.md): 返回一条凭据的非秘密设置。秘密值不返回。已归档的凭据仍可读取。
- [删除凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/删除凭据.md): 永久删除一条已归档的凭据。凭据必须先归档（否则返回 400 `failed_precondition_error`）。需要保留记录时请使用归档。
- [更新凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/更新凭据.md): 重命名凭据或轮换其秘密设置。
- [归档凭据](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/归档凭据.md): 归档凭据，清除其秘密值并释放其唯一键，可用于新建替代凭据。已归档的凭据不再对会话可用，但仍可读取。
- [创建 OAuth 会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/创建-oauth-会话.md): 为一个 MCP 服务器发起 OAuth 授权流程，并返回需在浏览器中打开的 URL。完成授权会在凭据库（Vault）中创建一条 `mcp_oauth` 凭据。
- [获取 OAuth 会话](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api-reference/凭据库/获取-oauth-会话.md): 返回 OAuth 授权流程的当前状态：进行中为 `pending`。成功为 `authorized`，并携带已创建的 `credential_id`。失败为 `failed`，并携带人类可读的 `error`。未知或已过期的 OAuth 会话返回 404。
