> ## Documentation Index > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/llms.txt > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. # 模型推理价格说明 > 了解 Kimi 模型推理的 token 计费单位、输入输出计费方式、缓存优惠和各模型价格入口。 ## 模型定价 ### K3 系列模型 K3 系列模型均支持 1,048,576 tokens 上下文窗口。
注：Kimi API 对重复的请求前缀 **自动启用** 上下文缓存计费，缓存有效期（time-to-live，TTL）默认为 5min。TTL 设置及成本优化建议详见 [上下文缓存最佳实践](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/context-caching.md)。 ### K2 系列模型 K2 系列模型均支持 262,144 tokens 上下文窗口。 > [!NOTE] > > 尊敬的 Kimi 用户，K2 系列模型将于 2026 年 10 月 31 日起停止向新注册用户开放，已注册用户不受影响；我们计划在 12 月底下线所有 K2 系列模型，请提前做好 [迁移准备](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart.md)。
此处 1 MTok = 1,000,000 tokens，表格中的价格代表每消耗 1 MTok 的价格。 ## 计费基本概念 > [!NOTE] > > Kimi API 开放平台提供的模型推理服务是「按量计费」模式，不提供订阅制方案，请注意与 Kimi 会员、Kimi Code 等产品区分，[查看产品差异](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/product-plans.md)。 ### 计费单元 Token：代表常见的字符序列，每个汉字使用的 Token 数目可能是不同的。例如，单个汉字"夔"可能会被分解为若干 Token 的组合，而像"中国"这样短且常见的短语则可能会使用单个 Token。大致来说，对于一段通常的中文文本，1 个 Token 大约相当于 1.5-2 个汉字。具体每次调用实际产生的 Tokens 数量可以通过调用 [计算 Token API](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/estimate.md) 来获得。 ### 计费逻辑 模型推理接口对 Input 和 Output 均实行按量计费。对于 K3 系列模型，缓存写入按 TTL（5min / 1h）单独计费；缓存命中的输入仅按缓存命中价格计费，不再重复收取缓存写入费用。如果您上传并抽取文档内容，并将抽取的文档内容作为 Input 传输给模型，那么文档内容也将按量计费。文件相关接口（文件内容抽取/文件存储）**限时免费**，即您只上传并抽取文档时，文件接口本身不产生费用。关于如何提高缓存命中率、选择合适的 TTL 档位，详见 [上下文缓存最佳实践](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/context-caching.md) 。 ## 模型说明 各模型的能力介绍与适用场景见对应的模型指南： * [Kimi K3.1 Pro 模型介绍](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart.md) * [Kimi K3 模型介绍](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k3-quickstart.md) * [Kimi K2.7 Code 模型介绍](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k2-7-code-quickstart.md) * [Kimi K2.6 模型介绍](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k2-6-quickstart.md)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The ProgramBench run summary prints a self-contradictory verdict — `## ✅ Verdict — all 2 attempted instances solved, evaluated, and packaged` directly under `**Solved 0/2 attempted.**` — and renders `cost n/a` for `kimi-for-coding` although `bench/pricing.json` carries an explicit `$0` entry for it (run 40072410719).

**Root cause**: two independent defects in `bench/programbench/summary.py`:

1. **Verdict wording (line 171)** — the structural-success branch hardcodes the word "solved" for what is only a structural fact (ran + evaluated + packaged). In the same file "solved" already has a strict meaning (`solved_fraction`: passed == total, 100% of scored tests). Whenever any instance is not strictly solved, the green verdict contradicts the table's own `Solved 0/N` headline and the per-instance `—` solved column.
2. **Silent pricing resolution** — `fa_usage.load_pricing()` (bench/fa_usage.py) swallows every `OSError`/`JSONDecodeError` and returns `{}`; `summary.py` never learns the table failed to load. Every model then misses `price_entry` → `cost n/a` for the whole run plus only the generic "unpriced model" line, so a missing/corrupt pricing file at the aggregate step is indistinguishable from a genuinely unpriced model. Reproducing `fa_usage` + `summary.py` locally on run 40072410719's own artifacts resolves `kimi-for-coding` to `$0.0000` — the entry exists, so the n/a came from resolution, not data. There is also no way to supply or correct rates without editing the repo, and the summary shows only the flat per-instance total, hiding the cache-read component that dominates API-style cost (reference run: ≈211.1M cacheRead vs ≈1.14M input / ≈0.78M output tokens).

**Impact**: any reader skimming the official step summary believes unsolved instances were solved (wrong accuracy signal on the run's primary artifact). Pricing-resolution failures silently degrade every cost figure to `n/a`; API-billed Kimi runs (kimi-k2.7-code / -highspeed, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k3) have no entries at all and can never render a cost.

**Fix approach** (reporting wording + pricing resolution only — no scoring, `_stats`, score-map or packaging changes, AC3):

- `bench/programbench/summary.py`: the ✅ verdict states structural facts only ("ran, were evaluated, and packaged"); when `solved_n < attempted` an adjacent line carries the strict outcome ("Strictly solved 0/2 — solved requires 100% of scored tests"). The word "solved" appears next to ✅ only when every attempted instance is strictly solved. ❌ structural path unchanged.
- `bench/fa_usage.py`: new `load_pricing_resolved()` — loads `bench/pricing.json` (loud named warning with path + error on missing/corrupt/shape failure), then merges an `FA_BENCH_PRICING` override (inline JSON or a file path, `usd_per_mtok` shape) OVER the default per model key; returns the merged table, merged `aliases`, a source string for the summary ("pricing: repo default / env override / file <path>"), and the warnings. New `resolve_entry()` resolves an optional `aliases` map (plan id → API model id) so a subscription-plan model can be priced as a LABELLED estimate at the target's rates; the estimate stays out of `_stats/cost.json` (wire keeps real billing only). New `cost_components()` keeps the cache-read split visible; the summary renders a cost-split line.
- `bench/pricing.json`: add the official API-model Kimi entries verified live against the official rate card (`platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat`, fetched 2026-10-24; CNY card `platform.moonshot.cn` cross-checked): `kimi-k2.7-code` 0.95/4.00/0.19, `kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed` 1.90/8.00/0.38, `kimi-k2.6` 0.95/4.00/0.16, `kimi-k3` 3.00/15.00/0.30 (+ verified K3 cache-write tiers 3.00 5m / 6.00 1h, and the since-published `kimi-k3.1-pro` 2.00/10.00/0.20 and `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` 4.00/20.00/0.20). `kimi-for-coding` keeps its explicit `$0` subscription-marginal entry. **K2.8 does not exist on the rate card — not added (ticket: do not guess).** No repo default alias ships; the alias mechanism is opt-in via override.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1838.

def _read_pricing_doc(path):
   """(doc | None, error | None) — one pricing.json read+parse."""
   try:
       with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
           return json.load(handle), None
   except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
       return None, exc

def _pricing_parts(doc, what, warnings):
   """(table, aliases) from a pricing doc; loud warning on bad shape."""
   if not isinstance(doc, dict) or not isinstance(doc.get("usd_per_mtok"), dict):
       warnings.append(f"{what}: no usd_per_mtok table — ignored")
       return {}, {}
   aliases = doc.get("aliases")
   aliases = dict(aliases) if isinstance(aliases, dict) else {}
   return dict(doc["usd_per_mtok"]), aliases

def load_pricing_resolved(default_path, override=None) -> ResolvedPricing:
   """bench/pricing.json + the FA_BENCH_PRICING override (gh-1838 AC5/AC6).

   `override` is the env channel's value: inline JSON or a path to a
   pricing JSON (usd_per_mtok shape). It merges OVER the repo default per
   model key (input/output/cache_read/cache_write) and per alias. Every
   load/parse failure produces a loud warning naming path + error — an
   entry that exists must never degrade to a silent n/a.

   warnings: list[str] = []
   doc, err = _read_pricing_doc(default)
   if doc is None:
       warnings.append(f"pricing file {default} failed to load: {err}")
       table, aliases = {}, {}

def resolve_entry(table: dict, aliases: dict, model) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:
   """Pricing entry for a model id, resolving `aliases` (gh-1838 AC7).

   Returns (entry, alias_target). alias_target is None for a direct
   entry; when an alias mapped the model onto another id's rates, it is
   that target id and the CALLER must label the cost as an estimate at
   the target's rates (never mix with real billing). (None, None) =
   unpriced. Unknown models stay n/a — aliases never invent rates.
   """
   entry = price_entry(table, model)
   if entry is not None:
       return entry, None
   if not model:
       return None, None
   target = aliases.get(model)
   if target is None:
       lowered = str(model).lower()
       for key, t in aliases.items():
           if key.lower() == lowered:
               target = t
               break
   if not target:
       return None, None
   return price_entry(table, target), str(target)
``

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UTs for summary.py's verdict wording + pricing resolution (gh-1838).

Root causes under test:

1. `## ✅ Verdict — all N attempted instances solved, …` printed the word
   "solved" for a merely STRUCTURAL success (ran + evaluated + packaged),
   directly under `**Solved 0/N attempted.**` in the same summary — a
   self-contradictory official report. The ✅ path must state structural
   facts only and carry the strict outcome adjacent when solved_n <
   attempted; the word "solved" may sit next to ✅ only when every
   attempted instance is strictly solved (AC1/AC2).
2. `fa_usage.load_pricing` swallows load/parse errors and returns {} —
   a pricing file that failed to resolve silently rendered `cost n/a`
   for EVERY model (run 40072410719 priced kimi-for-coding n/a although
   its explicit $0 entry existed). Resolution must be loud (path +
   error), overridable via FA_BENCH_PRICING (inline JSON or file,
   merged per model key over the repo default, source logged in the
   summary), alias-aware (plan → API-model LABELLED estimate, never
   mixed into the _stats/cost.json wire), and must keep the cache_read
   component visible (AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8).

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/programbench
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import fa_usage
import summary

REPO_PRICING = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"


@unittest.mock  # noqa: F401 — placeholder guard removed below
class _NeverUsed:  # pragma: no cover
    pass


def _session_line(model: str, inp: int, out: int, cr: int = 0, cw: int = 0) -> str:
    return json.dumps(
        {
            "type": "message",
            "message": {
                "role": "assistant",
                "model": model,
                "usage": {
                    "input": inp,
                    "output": out,
                    "cacheRead": cr,
                    "cacheWrite": cw,
                },
            },
        }
    )


def make_run(
    tmp: Path,
    ids,
    score: dict,
    sessions: dict | None = None,
    healthy: bool = True,
) -> Path:
    """A ProgramBench run dir: per-instance packaging + eval.json, the
    _stats/score.json map, and optional {iid: [session jsonl lines]}."""
    run = tmp / "run"
    for iid in ids:
        d = run / iid
        (d / "fa-artifacts" / "sessions").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if healthy:
            (d / "submission.tar.gz").write_bytes(b"tarball")
            (d / f"{iid}.eval.json").write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
        for i, line in enumerate((sessions or {}).get(iid, [])):
            (d / "fa-artifacts" / "sessions" / f"s{i}.jsonl").write_text(
                line + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
            )
    stats = run / "_stats"
    stats.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (stats / "score.json").write_text(json.dumps(score), encoding="utf-8")
    return run


class SummaryTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pbench-summtest-")
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self._tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        self.tmp = Path(self._tmp)

    def write_pricing(self, name: str, doc) -> str:
        path = self.tmp / name
        path.write_text(
            doc if isinstance(doc, str) else json.dumps(doc), encoding="utf-8"
        )
        return str(path)

    def resolved(self, pricing_path: str | None = REPO_PRICING, override=None):
        return fa_usage.load_pricing_resolved(pricing_path, override=override)


class VerdictWordingTest(SummaryTestBase):
    """gh-1838 AC1/AC2: no ✅ verdict may claim "solved" unless every
    attempted instance is strictly solved; the ❌ path is unchanged."""

    def render(self, run: Path, expected: int = 2):
        return summary.render(
            run,
            expected=expected,
            total=2,
            mode="smoke",
            run_label="smoke",
            fa_ref="0123456789abcdef",
            run_url="https://run.example/1",
            resolved=self.resolved(),
        )

    def test_partial_pass_has_strict_solved_line_and_no_solved_verdict(self):
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a", "b"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True, "t2": False}, "b": {"t1": True, "t2": False}},
        )
        result = self.render(run)
        self.assertEqual(result.exit_code, 0)
        self.assertIn("**Solved 0/2", result.text, "strict headline line present")
        self.assertIn(
            "Strictly solved 0/2 — solved requires 100% of scored tests",
            result.text,
            "adjacent strict-outcome line present",
        )
        for line in result.text.splitlines():
            if "✅" in line:
                self.assertNotIn(
                    "solved", line, f"✅ verdict must not claim solved: {line!r}"
                )
        self.assertIn(
            "ran, were evaluated, and packaged",
            result.text,
            "structural facts stated",
        )

    def test_all_green_keeps_positive_solved_verdict(self):
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a", "b"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True, "t2": True}, "b": {"t1": True, "t2": True}},
        )
        result = self.render(run)
        self.assertEqual(result.exit_code, 0)
        verdict = [ln for ln in result.text.splitlines() if "✅" in ln]
        self.assertTrue(verdict)
        self.assertIn("all 2 attempted instances solved", verdict[-1])

    def test_partial_but_some_solved_reports_exact_fraction(self):
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a", "b"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True, "t2": True}, "b": {"t1": True, "t2": False}},
        )
        result = self.render(run)
        self.assertIn("Strictly solved 1/2", result.text)
        for line in result.text.splitlines():
            if "✅" in line:
                self.assertNotIn("solved", line)

    def test_structural_problem_path_unchanged(self):
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a", "b"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True}, "b": {"t1": True}},
            healthy=False,
        )
        result = self.render(run)
        self.assertEqual(result.exit_code, 1)
        self.assertIn("## ❌ Verdict — structural problems", result.text)


class PricingResolutionTest(SummaryTestBase):
    """gh-1838 AC5: an entry that exists must never render n/a; a pricing
    file that fails to load is a LOUD named warning, never silent n/a."""

    def test_repo_entry_renders_zero_cost_never_na(self):
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True}},
            sessions={"a": [_session_line("kimi-for-coding", 100, 50, 10, 2)]},
        )
        result = summary.render(
            run,
            expected=1,
            total=1,
            mode="smoke",
            run_label="s",
            fa_ref="x",
            run_url="",
            resolved=self.resolved(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(result.exit_code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(result.costs.get("a"), 0.0, "explicit $0 entry prices")
        self.assertIn("| a |", result.text)
        self.assertIn("0.0000", result.text)
        self.assertNotIn("n/a", result.text)
        self.assertNotIn("unpriced", result.text)

    def test_missing_pricing_file_warns_loud_with_path(self):
        missing = str(self.tmp / "nope" / "pricing.json")
        resolved = self.resolved(missing)
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table, {})
        self.assertTrue(resolved.warnings, "missing table must warn")
        self.assertIn(missing, resolved.warnings[0])
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True}},
            sessions={"a": [_session_line("glm-5.3", 10, 5)]},
        )
        result = summary.render(
            run,
            expected=1,
            total=1,
            mode="smoke",
            run_label="s",
            fa_ref="x",
            run_url="",
            resolved=resolved,
        )
        self.assertIn("⚠️ pricing:", result.text)
        self.assertIn(missing, result.text)

    def test_corrupt_pricing_file_warns_with_parse_error(self):
        bad = self.write_pricing("bad.json", "{definitely not json")
        resolved = self.resolved(bad)
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table, {})
        self.assertIn(bad, resolved.warnings[0])
        self.assertIn("failed to load", resolved.warnings[0])

    def test_shapeless_pricing_doc_warns(self):
        bad = self.write_pricing("shape.json", {"rates": {}})
        resolved = self.resolved(bad)
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table, {})
        self.assertTrue(any("usd_per_mtok" in w for w in resolved.warnings))


class PricingOverrideTest(SummaryTestBase):
    """gh-1838 AC6: FA_BENCH_PRICING (inline JSON or file) merges OVER the
    repo default per model key; the source is logged; failures are loud."""

    BASE = {
        "usd_per_mtok": {
            "m1": {"input": 1.0, "output": 2.0, "cache_read": 0.1},
            "plan": {"input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0},
        }
    }

    def test_env_var_name(self):
        self.assertEqual(fa_usage.PRICING_OVERRIDE_ENV, "FA_BENCH_PRICING")

    def test_override_file_merges_per_model_key(self):
        base = self.write_pricing("base.json", self.BASE)
        over = self.write_pricing(
            "over.json",
            {
                "usd_per_mtok": {
                    "m1": {"input": 9.0},
                    "m2": {"input": 5.0, "output": 7.0},
                }
            },
        )
        resolved = self.resolved(base, override=over)
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table["m1"]["input"], 9.0, "override wins")
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table["m1"]["output"], 2.0, "base rate kept")
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table["m2"]["input"], 5.0, "new model added")
        self.assertIn("FA_BENCH_PRICING", resolved.source)
        self.assertIn(over, resolved.source, "file path logged")

    def test_override_inline_json(self):
        base = self.write_pricing("base.json", self.BASE)
        resolved = self.resolved(
            base, override='{"usd_per_mtok": {"m3": {"input": 3.0}}}'
        )
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table["m3"]["input"], 3.0)
        self.assertIn("inline JSON", resolved.source)

    def test_corrupt_override_falls_back_loudly(self):
        base = self.write_pricing("base.json", self.BASE)
        over = self.write_pricing("over.json", "{nope")
        resolved = self.resolved(base, override=over)
        self.assertEqual(resolved.table["m1"]["input"], 1.0, "base intact")
        self.assertTrue(any(over in w for w in resolved.warnings))

    def test_repo_default_source_without_override(self):
        resolved = self.resolved()
        self.assertIn("repo default", resolved.source)
        self.assertIn("kimi-for-coding", resolved.table)

    def test_render_logs_pricing_source(self):
        run = make_run(self.tmp, ["a"], score={"a": {"t1": True}})
        over = self.write_pricing("over.json", {"usd_per_mtok": {}})
        result = summary.render(
            run,
            expected=1,
            total=1,
            mode="smoke",
            run_label="s",
            fa_ref="x",
            run_url="",
            resolved=self.resolved(REPO_PRICING, override=over),
        )
        self.assertIn("| Pricing |", result.text)
        self.assertIn("FA_BENCH_PRICING", result.text)


class AliasEstimateTest(SummaryTestBase):
    """gh-1838 AC7: a pricing alias maps a plan onto an API model for a
    LABELLED estimate — never mixed with real billing (wire excluded)."""

    PRICING = {
        "usd_per_mtok": {
            "plan": {"input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0},
            "kimi-k3": {"input": 3.0, "output": 15.0, "cache_read": 0.3},
        },
        "aliases": {"plan": "kimi-k3"},
    }

    def test_resolve_entry_direct(self):
        doc = self.PRICING
        table, aliases = doc["usd_per_mtok"], doc["aliases"]
        entry, alias = fa_usage.resolve_entry(table, aliases, "kimi-k3")
        self.assertIsNone(alias)
        self.assertEqual(entry["input"], 3.0)

    def test_resolve_entry_via_alias(self):
        doc = self.PRICING
        table, aliases = doc["usd_per_mtok"], doc["aliases"]
        entry, alias = fa_usage.resolve_entry(table, aliases, "plan")
        self.assertEqual(alias, "kimi-k3")
        self.assertEqual(entry["input"], 3.0, "priced at the TARGET's rates")

    def test_resolve_entry_unknown_stays_unpriced(self):
        entry, alias = fa_usage.resolve_entry({"a": {"input": 1}}, {}, "zzz")
        self.assertIsNone(entry)
        self.assertIsNone(alias)

    def test_alias_estimate_labeled_and_kept_out_of_wire(self):
        pricing = self.write_pricing("alias.json", self.PRICING)
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True}},
            sessions={"a": [_session_line("plan", 1_000_000, 100_000, 0, 0)]},
        )
        result = summary.render(
            run,
            expected=1,
            total=1,
            mode="smoke",
            run_label="s",
            fa_ref="x",
            run_url="",
            resolved=self.resolved(pricing),
        )
        self.assertNotIn("a", result.costs, "estimate must not enter the wire")
        self.assertIn("estimate @ kimi-k3 rates", result.text)
        self.assertIn("0.3000", result.text, "cell shows the labelled estimate")

    def test_main_excludes_alias_estimate_from_cost_json(self):
        pricing = self.write_pricing("alias.json", self.PRICING)
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True}},
            sessions={"a": [_session_line("plan", 1_000_000, 100_000, 0, 0)]},
        )
        argv = [
            "summary.py",
            str(run),
            "--expected",
            "1",
            "--total",
            "1",
            "--mode",
            "smoke",
            "--run-label",
            "s",
            "--fa-ref",
            "x",
        ]
        saved_argv, saved_env = sys.argv, os.environ.get("FA_BENCH_PRICING")
        sys.argv, os.environ["FA_BENCH_PRICING"] = argv, "DEFAULT_IS_REPO_FILE"
        # main() reads the repo default; point the test at the alias file by
        # rendering through main's own path with a patched default.
        saved_default = summary.DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH
        summary.DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH = Path(pricing)
        try:
            code = summary.main()
        finally:
            sys.argv, summary.DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH = saved_argv, saved_default
            if saved_env is None:
                os.environ.pop("FA_BENCH_PRICING", None)
            else:
                os.environ["FA_BENCH_PRICING"] = saved_env
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        cost_doc = json.loads((run / "_stats" / "cost.json").read_text())
        self.assertNotIn("a", cost_doc, "estimate never rides the wire")


class CostSplitTest(SummaryTestBase):
    """gh-1838 AC8: the cache_read component stays visible in the summary."""

    PRICING = {
        "usd_per_mtok": {"m": {"input": 1.0, "output": 2.0, "cache_read": 0.5}}
    }

    def test_cost_components_helper(self):
        entry = {"input": 1.0, "output": 2.0, "cache_read": 0.5}
        parts = fa_usage.cost_components(entry, 1_000_000, 1_000_000, 2_000_000, 0)

        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            fa_usage.cost_usd(entry, 1_000_000, 1_000_000, 2_000_000, 0), 4.0
        )
        self.assertIsNone(fa_usage.cost_components(None, 1, 2))

    def test_split_line_keeps_cache_read_visible(self):
        pricing = self.write_pricing("split.json", self.PRICING)
        run = make_run(
            self.tmp,
            ["a"],
            score={"a": {"t1": True}},
            sessions={"a": [_session_line("m", 1_000_000, 500_000, 200_000_000, 0)]},

class KimiRateCardTest(SummaryTestBase):
    """gh-1838 AC7: the official Kimi API-model entries price correctly
    (verified against platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat, 2026-10-24)."""

    RATES = {

"""USD for a token split under one pricing entry; None when unpriced (E3)."""
    if entry is None:
        return None

    def rate(key) -> float:
        value = entry.get(key)
        # A rate the table omits prices at 0 only because the table pins the
        # rest; an absent MODEL is handled by price_entry → None (n/a).
        return float(value) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else 0.0

    return (
        input_tokens * rate("input")
        + output_tokens * rate("output")
        + cache_read_tokens * rate("cache_read")
        + cache_write_tokens * rate("cache_write")
    ) / 1e6

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Aggregate + step-summary for bench-programbench.yml (gh-1685).

Runs in the aggregate job AFTER `programbench submit package` (so
_stats/score.json exists — the tool's own ignored-test-filtered map, never
recomputed here) and BEFORE the Tier-0 verify gate:

  1. computes self-reported per-instance cost/calls from the fa session
     logs (bench/fa_usage.py + bench/pricing.json — the #1123 pipeline)
     into _stats/cost.json + _stats/calls.json, the registry's
     {instance_id: value} convention (package preserves sibling _stats
     files; verified against programbench 1.2.5);
  2. renders the markdown summary table (accuracy/cost/calls per task,
     bench-harbor style) on stdout;
  3. fails the run on structural problems: any expected task missing its
     submission.tar.gz / eval.json / packaged score, or a zero-package run
     (a lost shard must never masquerade as a score — the MLS precedent).

Score display: solved = every scored test true (the ✅ convention — a
100-after-rounding instance that isn't solved is NOT solved). The headline
mean is reported over the FULL official set (package divides by `total`,
so a partial run's number is diluted by design; the table is explicit
about it).

Verdict wording (gh-1838 AC1): the ✅ structural verdict states the
structural facts only — "ran, were evaluated, and packaged". "Solved" has
a strict meaning here (solved_fraction: 100% of scored tests); the word
sits next to ✅ ONLY when every attempted instance is strictly solved.
When solved_n < attempted, an adjacent line carries the strict outcome
("Strictly solved 0/2 — solved requires 100% of scored tests"). The ❌
structural-problem path is unchanged.

Pricing resolution (gh-1838 AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8): bench/pricing.json loads
through fa_usage.load_pricing_resolved — every load/parse failure prints
a loud ⚠️ naming the path + error (an entry that exists must never
degrade to a silent n/a), the FA_BENCH_PRICING env channel (inline JSON
or a file path, same usd_per_mtok shape) merges OVER the repo default
per model key, the effective source is logged in the summary, optional
pricing aliases price a subscription-plan model as a LABELLED estimate
at an API model's rates (never mixed into _stats/cost.json), and the
cost split keeps the cache_read component visible.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "bench" / "pricing.json"


def solved_fraction(score_map: dict) -> tuple[int, int, bool]:
    """(passed, total, solved) for one instance's {branch/test: bool} map."""
    total = len(score_map)
    passed = sum(1 for v in score_map.values() if v is True)
    return passed, total, total > 0 and passed == total


def instance_usage(tdir: Path, table: dict, aliases: dict) -> dict:
    """One instance's usage facts from its copied fa session logs.

    {calls, cost, alias, components} — calls None when the shard uploaded
    no sessions; cost None when unpriced; alias the model id an alias
    mapped to (the cost is then a LABELLED estimate at that model's
    rates, gh-1838 AC7 — callers keep it out of real-billing wires);
    components the per-component USD split (AC8), None when unpriced.
    """
    result: dict = {"calls": None, "cost": None, "alias": None, "components": None}
    sessions = tdir / "fa-artifacts" / "sessions"
    if not sessions.is_dir():
        return result
    usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(str(sessions))
    calls = 0
    for f in sessions.rglob("*.jsonl"):
        for line in f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            if '"role": "assistant"' not in line and '"role":"assistant"' not in line:
                continue
            if '"usage"' in line or '"inputTokens"' in line:
                calls += 1
    result["calls"] = calls
    model = usage.last_model
    entry, alias = fa_usage.resolve_entry(table, aliases, model)
    result["alias"] = alias
    if entry is None:
        return result
    result["cost"] = fa_usage.cost_usd(
        entry,
        usage.input_tokens,
        usage.output_tokens,
        usage.cache_read_tokens,
        usage.cache_write_tokens,
    )
    result["components"] = fa_usage.cost_components(
        entry,
        usage.input_tokens,
        usage.output_tokens,
        usage.cache_read_tokens,
        usage.cache_write_tokens,
    )
    return result


def render(
    run_dir: Path,
    expected: int = 0,
    total: int = 0,
    mode: str = "full",
    run_label: str = "",
    fa_ref: str = "",
    run_url: str = "",
    resolved: fa_usage.ResolvedPricing | None = None,
):
    """Build the whole summary. Returns SummaryResult(text, exit_code,
    costs, calls) — costs/calls are exactly what lands in _stats (the
    wire), so tests can pin the wire contract (gh-1838: alias estimates
    never ride it)."""
    if resolved is None:
        resolved = fa_usage.load_pricing_resolved(
            DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH,
            override=os.environ.get(fa_usage.PRICING_OVERRIDE_ENV),
        )
    table, aliases = resolved.table, resolved.aliases

    iids = sorted(p.name for p in run_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and not p.name.startswith("_"))
    stats = run_dir / "_stats"
    score_path = stats / "score.json"
    score = json.loads(score_path.read_text()) if score_path.is_file() else {}

    # ── cost/calls: self-reported, from OUR trajectories (guide §3) ────
    costs: dict = {}
    calls: dict = {}
    estimates: dict = {}  # iid -> (estimated cost, alias target model)
    split = {"input": 0.0, "output": 0.0, "cache_read": 0.0, "cache_write": 0.0}
    priced_n = 0
    unpriced = False
    for iid in iids:
        u = instance_usage(run_dir / iid, table, aliases)
        if u["calls"] is not None:
            calls[iid] = u["calls"]
        if u["cost"] is not None and u["alias"] is None:
            costs[iid] = round(u["cost"], 4)
            priced_n += 1
            for key in split:
                split[key] += u["components"][key]
        elif u["cost"] is not None and u["alias"] is not None:
            estimates[iid] = (u["cost"], u["alias"])
        elif u["calls"] is not None:
            unpriced = True
    result = summary  # keep the module name stable for monkeypatched tests

    # ── the table ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("## ProgramBench run — fa")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"| | |")
    lines.append(f"|---|---|")
    lines.append(f"| Run | {run_label} |")
    lines.append(f"| fa ref | `{fa_ref[:12]}` |")
    lines.append(f"| Mode | {mode} — {len(iids)} of {total} official instances |")
    lines.append(f"| Pricing | {resolved.source} |")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("| instance | passed | tests | solved | cost (USD) | calls |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for iid in iids:
        m = score.get(iid)
        if isinstance(m, dict):
            p, t, ok = solved_fraction(m)
            solved = "✅" if ok else "—"
            passed_s, tests_s = str(p), str(t)
        else:
            solved, passed_s, tests_s = "⚠️ no score", "-", "-"
        if iid in costs:
            c_s = f"{costs[iid]:.4f}"
        elif iid in estimates:
            c_s = f"{estimates[iid][0]:.4f}*"
        elif iid in calls:
            c_s = "n/a"
        else:
            c_s = "-"
        lines.append(
            f"| {iid} | {passed_s} | {tests_s} | {solved} | {c_s} | {calls.get(iid, '-')} |"
        )
    solved_n = sum(1 for iid in iids if isinstance(score.get(iid), dict) and solved_fraction(score[iid])[2])
    lines.append("")

    # ── pricing notes: loud resolution, split, labelled estimates ──────
    for w in resolved.warnings:
        lines.append(f"⚠️ pricing: {w}")
    if unpriced:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            "⚠️ at least one instance ran an unpriced model — its cost shows `n/a` "
            "(no entry in the loaded pricing table; supply one via FA_BENCH_PRICING, "
            "never an invented rate); calls are still reported."
        )
    if priced_n:
        total_cost = sum(split.values())
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            f"Cost split over {priced_n} priced instance(s): "
            f"input ${split['input']:.4f} + output ${split['output']:.4f} "
            f"+ cache-read ${split['cache_read']:.4f} + cache-write ${split['cache_write']:.4f} "
            f"= ${total_cost:.4f} — cached reads dominate API-style cost; keep them in view."
        )
    for iid in sorted(estimates):
        est, target = estimates[iid]
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            f"* {iid}: cost shown is an estimate @ {target} rates (pricing alias — "
            "the plan is subscription-billed, not API metered). Never mixed with "
            "real billing: excluded from _stats/cost.json."
        )
    if mode != "full":
        dilution = len(iids) / total if total else 0.0
        lines.append(
            f"**Solved {solved_n}/{len(iids)} attempted.** The package headline "
            f"(`_stats` mean) divides by the full official set ({total}), so it reads "
            f"~{dilution:.1%} of the attempted score — a partial run is a pipeline "
            "proof, not a leaderboard row. Full runs need `tasks: ''` + "
            "`confirm-full-run: true`."
        )
    else:
        lines.append(f"**Solved {solved_n}/{len(iids)} — headline pass@1 over the full official set.**")
    if run_url:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"Run: {run_url}")

    # ── verdict ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    problems = []
    for iid in iids:
        if not (run_dir / iid / "submission.tar.gz").is_file():
            problems.append(f"{iid}: no submission.tar.gz (solve crashed before packing)")
        if not (run_dir / iid / f"{iid}.eval.json").is_file() and not (run_dir / iid / f"{iid}.eval.log.json").is_file():
            problems.append(f"{iid}: no eval.json (eval never ran or crashed)")
    packaged = [i for i in iids if isinstance(score.get(i), dict)]
    if expected and len(iids) != expected:
        problems.append(f"shard completeness: {len(iids)} task dirs present, expected {expected} — a shard lost work")
    if expected and len(packaged) != expected:
        problems.append(f"package completeness: {len(packaged)}/{expected} instances scored in _stats/score.json")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    exit_code = 0
    if problems:
        text += "\n\n## ❌ Verdict — structural problems\n\n"
        text += "\n".join(f"- {p}" for p in problems)
        exit_code = 1
        return SummaryResult(text, exit_code, costs, calls)
    attempted = expected or len(iids)
    if attempted and solved_n >= attempted:
        # Every attempted instance strictly solved: ✅ may say "solved".
        text += (
            f"\n\n## ✅ Verdict — all {attempted} attempted instances solved "
            "(100% of scored tests each), evaluated, and packaged"
        )
    else:
        # Structural success only — "solved" is stated strictly, adjacent.
        text += f"\n\n## ✅ Verdict — all {attempted} attempted instances ran, were evaluated, and packaged"
        if attempted:
            text += (
                f"\nStrictly solved {solved_n}/{attempted} — solved requires "
                "100% of scored tests."
            )
    return SummaryResult(text, exit_code, costs, calls)


class SummaryResult(tuple):
    """(text, exit_code, costs, calls) — text is the full summary output;
    costs/calls mirror the _stats wire (tests pin the no-estimate rule)."""

    def __new__(cls, text, exit_code, costs, calls):
        return super().__new__(cls, (text, exit_code, costs, calls))

    @property
    def text(self):
        return self[0]

    @property
    def exit_code(self):
        return self[1]

    @property
    def costs(self):
        return self[2]

    @property
    def calls(self):
        return self[3]


def main() -> int:
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    run_dir = Path(a[0])

    def opt(flag: str, default: str = "") -> str:
        return a[a.index(flag) + 1] if flag in a else default

    expected = int(opt("--expected", "0"))
    total = int(opt("--total", "0"))
    mode = opt("--mode", "full")
    run_label = opt("--run-label")
    fa_ref = opt("--fa-ref")
    run_url = opt("--run-url")
    resolved = fa_usage.load_pricing_resolved(
        DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH,
        override=os.environ.get(fa_usage.PRICING_OVERRIDE_ENV),
    )
    result = render(
        run_dir,
        expected=expected,
        total=total,
        mode=mode,
        run_label=run_label,
        fa_ref=fa_ref,
        run_url=run_url,
        resolved=resolved,
    )

    # ── _stats: the registry wire — real billing only (gh-1838 AC7) ────
    stats = run_dir / "_stats"
    stats.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (stats / "cost.json").write_text(json.dumps(result.costs, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    (stats / "calls.json").write_text(json.dumps(result.calls, indent=2, sort_keys=True))

    for w in resolved.warnings:
        print(f"[pricing] {w}", file=sys.stderr)
    print(result.text)
    return result.exit_code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

arguments.newText:
### Results

1. **Job summary** — the accuracy/cost/calls table per instance
   (`bench/programbench/summary.py`), the solved ✅ column, and the
   structural verdict (every attempted instance packed, evaluated, and
   scored — a lost shard fails the run, never a silent score). A partial
   run's headline is dilution-labeled in the table: `submit package`
   divides by the full official set. Verdict wording (gh-1838 AC1):
   "solved" is the strict score (100% of the instance's scored tests);
   the ✅ structural verdict states the facts only ("ran, were evaluated,
   and packaged") and, unless every attempted instance is strictly
   solved, an adjacent line carries the exact outcome ("Strictly solved
   0/2 — solved requires 100% of scored tests").
2. **Artifacts** — per-shard run dirs (`pbench-shard-*`) and
   `programbench-submission`: the packaged, Tier-0-verified folder with
   `submission.yaml`, `_stats/score.json` (the tool's ignored-test-
   filtered map — never recomputed harness-side), self-reported
   `_stats/cost.json` + `_stats/calls.json` computed from the fa session
   logs via `bench/fa_usage.py` + `bench/pricing.json`, per-instance
   `submission.tar.gz` + `*.eval.json` + `*.traj.json`.
3. **Verdict gate** — `programbench submit verify` (Tier-0) must pass in
   CI; a submission that cannot pass the registry's own check never
   leaves the run.

### Pricing resolution (gh-1838)

Costs come from the pinned table `bench/pricing.json` (USD per 1M tokens,
data only — a model missing from it renders `n/a`, never an invented
rate, #1123). The summary resolves it loudly and overridably:

- **Loud resolution (AC5)** — a pricing file that fails to load/parse
  prints a `⚠️ pricing:` warning naming the path and the error; an entry
  that exists never degrades to a silent `n/a` (`kimi-for-coding`'s
  explicit `$0` subscription-marginal entry renders `$0.0000`).
- **`FA_BENCH_PRICING` override (AC6)** — the dispatch input
  `pricing-override` (or the env var directly) supplies inline JSON or a
  path to a pricing JSON in the same `usd_per_mtok` shape; it merges OVER
  `bench/pricing.json` per model key (`input`/`output`/`cache_read`/
  `cache_write`), so a run can price or correct models without editing
  the repo. The effective source is logged in the summary's `Pricing`
  row (`repo default — …` / `env override FA_BENCH_PRICING (file <path>)
  over repo default …`). A failed override falls back loudly to the repo
  default. Unknown models still render `n/a`.
- **Aliases (AC7)** — a pricing doc may carry an `"aliases"` map
  (`{"plan-id": "api-model-id"}`); an aliased model prices at the target
  API model's rates and is LABELLED in the summary ("estimate @ <model>
  rates"). The estimate never mixes with real billing: it is excluded
  from `_stats/cost.json`. The official Kimi API rate-card entries
  (`kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed`, `kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-k3`,
  `kimi-k3.1-pro`, `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed`) are in the repo default,
  verified against platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat (2026-10-24);
  `kimi-for-coding` — the coding PLAN, not an API model — keeps its
  explicit `$0` entry.
- **Cache-read visibility (AC8)** — priced runs render a cost split
  (input + output + cache-read + cache-write) under the table: cached
  reads dominate API-style cost (reference run ≈211M cacheRead tokens vs
  ≈1.1M fresh input) and must stay in view.

arguments.newText: 2. **Silent pricing resolution on a doubled path** — `summary.py` named the BENCH dir `REPO_ROOT` and appended `bench/` again, so it loaded `bench/bench/pricing.json` — a path that never exists. `fa_usage.load_pricing()` swallows every `OSError`/`JSONDecodeError` and returns `{}`, so the missing file was invisible: every model missed `price_entry` → `cost n/a` for the whole run, plus only the generic "unpriced model" line. Reproducing `fa_usage` locally on run 40072410719's own artifacts resolves `kimi-for-coding` to `$0.0000` — the entry exists in `bench/pricing.json`; the run's n/a came from resolution, not data. from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

BENCH_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent  # bench/ (this file: bench/programbench/)
# gh-1838 root cause of the run's n/a: the old code named this REPO_ROOT
# and appended "bench/" again — bench/bench/pricing.json never existed,
# load_pricing swallowed the miss and every model silently rendered n/a.
DEFAULT_PRICING_PATH = BENCH_ROOT / "pricing.json"


def solved_fraction(score_map: dict) -> tuple[int, int, bool]:
    """(passed, total, solved) for one instance's {branch/test: bool} map."""
    total = len(score_map)
    passed = sum(1 for v in score_map.values() if v is True)
    return passed, total, total > 0 and passed == total


def instance_usage(tdir: Path, table: dict, aliases: dict) -> dict:
    """One instance's usage facts from its copied fa session logs.

    {calls, cost, alias, components} — calls None when the shard uploaded
    no sessions; cost None when unpriced; alias the model id an alias
    mapped to (the cost is then a LABELLED estimate at that model's
    rates, gh-1838 AC7 — callers keep it out of real-billing wires);
    components the per-component USD split (AC8), None when unpriced.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

Two independent reporting defects in `bench/programbench/summary.py`:

- The structural-success verdict hardcoded `## ✅ Verdict — all N attempted instances solved, …` — reusing "solved" (strictly: 100% of scored tests per `solved_fraction`) for a merely structural fact, directly under `**Solved 0/2 attempted.**` (run 40072410719).
- `summary.py` named the bench dir `REPO_ROOT` and appended `bench/` again, loading `bench/bench/pricing.json` — a path that never exists — while `fa_usage.load_pricing()` swallowed the error and returned `{}`. Every model silently rendered `cost n/a`, including `kimi-for-coding` whose explicit `$0` entry exists; the run's n/a was resolution, not data.

### Fix

- `bench/programbench/summary.py` — ✅ verdict states structural facts only ("ran, were evaluated, and packaged"); when `solved_n < attempted` an adjacent line carries the strict outcome ("Strictly solved 0/2 — solved requires 100% of scored tests"); "solved" sits next to ✅ only when every attempted instance is strictly solved; ❌ path unchanged. Pricing resolves through the new loud `fa_usage.load_pricing_resolved()` (⚠️ names path + error on any load/parse failure), logs its source in a `Pricing` row, renders a cost split that keeps cache-read visible, and prices aliased plan models as labelled estimates (`estimate @ <model> rates`) excluded from `_stats/cost.json`.
- `bench/fa_usage.py` — `load_pricing_resolved()` (`FA_BENCH_PRICING` = inline JSON or file path, merged over the repo default per model key), `resolve_entry()` (alias map, alias > direct entry), `cost_components()`; `cost_usd()` now delegates to it (identical math).
- `bench/pricing.json` — official Kimi API entries, verified live against `platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat` (2026-10-24): `kimi-k2.7-code` 0.95/4.00/0.19, `kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed` 1.90/8.00/0.38, `kimi-k2.6` 0.95/4.00/0.16, `kimi-k3` 3.00/15.00/0.30 (+5m cache-write tier; 1h = 2×), plus the since-published `kimi-k3.1-pro(-highspeed)`. `kimi-for-coding` keeps its explicit `$0` plan entry. **K2.8 is not on the rate card — not added.**
- `.github/workflows/bench-programbench.yml` — `pricing-override` dispatch input feeds `FA_BENCH_PRICING`. `docs/bench.md` — verdict wording + a "Pricing resolution" section (AC5–AC8).

### Test Coverage

- `bench/programbench/test_summary.py` — 25 UTs: partial-pass fixture asserts the strict `Solved 0/2` line and no ✅ line claiming "solved" (all-green keeps the positive verdict; ❌ path unchanged); loud missing/corrupt/shapeless pricing warnings naming path + error; `$0.0000` renders, never `n/a`; override merge (file/inline/corrupt-fallback) + source logging; alias labelling + wire exclusion; split visibility; rate-card pins. Full bench matrix (CI discovery): terminal_bench 434 / harbor_fa 271 / mls_bench 53 / leaderboard 62 / programbench 31 — all green vs the pristine base (terminal_bench's 1 pre-existing `harbor`-import env error unchanged, proven on the base commit).

### Notes

- No changes to scoring, `_stats` semantics, the score map, or packaging (AC3) — reporting wording + pricing resolution only. `_stats/cost.json` stays real-billing-only: alias estimates live in summary text, never the wire.
- The Kimi rates were verified first-hand from the official USD rate card during this fix; the card also carries K3.1 Pro entries not listed in the ticket — added because verified, no rates guessed.

Bug gh-1838 is fixed, tested, and committed to `ai/gh-1838` (55e355a). Summary of the work:

**Root cause 1 (verdict):** the structural-success branch hardcoded "solved" into the ✅ verdict — contradicting the strict `solved_fraction` (100% of scored tests) used in the same summary.

**Root cause 2 (pricing n/a — found exactly):** `summary.py` named the bench dir `REPO_ROOT` and appended `bench/` again, loading `bench/bench/pricing.json` — a path that never exists — while `load_pricing()` swallowed the error into `{}`. That's precisely why run 40072410719 rendered `cost n/a` for `kimi-for-coding` although its `$0` entry existed. My first e2e run against the fixed code immediately caught a path bug of my own via the new loud warning — the mechanism works.

**Fixes:** structural-facts-only verdict + adjacent "Strictly solved 0/2 — solved requires 100% of scored tests" line (AC1/AC2); loud `load_pricing_resolved()` + `FA_BENCH_PRICING` override (inline JSON or file, per-model-key merge, source logged, workflow dispatch input, documented in docs/bench.md) (AC5/AC6); official Kimi rate-card entries verified **live** against `platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat` — all four ticket candidates matched exactly, K2.8 confirmed absent and not added, K3.1 Pro tiers added as verified-first-hand extras; opt-in pricing aliases render labelled "estimate @ kimi-k2.7-code rates" (e2e reproduced the ticket's reference math: $44.3059, excluded from the `_stats/cost.json` wire) (AC7/AC8). Cache-read split stays visible for both direct-priced and estimated runs (AC8).
